description:
The citation map of issue 554c2935 finds prose citations by a pattern list, and its record states that a prose citation in a form the list does not match appears in no section. A read of every comment and Rustdoc line closes that gap for the source-comment sweep.

## Background

The holistic review of story ffc35b8c on 2026-10-04 found that the map cannot establish that every external work cited in a Rust comment has a registry key. The map, its script and its scope and edition rules are `554c2935-citation-map.md`, `554c2935-citation-map.py` and `554c2935-citation-map.txt` in the epic's directory; the registry is `.jit/references.toml`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A linked record names the commit read and lists, for each tracked Rust file under `crates/` and `dev/tools/`, the number of comment and Rustdoc lines read and each line that names an external work under the map's scope rule; the lines read are those the citation map script reads, and the per-crate totals of lines that begin with `//` equal the comment counts of the sweep census at that commit.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each external work the read finds that the citation map lists in no section has a registry entry with bibliographic data verified against the publisher, the archive or the standards body, a row in the map script's tables, and its `@/citation/<key>` address in the citing comment; a work that cannot be identified is listed in the map's section of citations without a registry entry.
- [hard] REQ-03: The citation map is regenerated, its script exits with status 0, and its record states that its coverage rests on the pattern list and on this read.
- [hard] REQ-04: Rust source changes are comment and Rustdoc edits only, and the Rust CI gate passes.
title: Read every Rust comment line for citations the map's patterns miss
